skill.name: agile-design-doc

content.value_statement: Agile teams often need design docs that are useful but not oversized. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to produce MVP-focused technical design documents.
actual_capabilities: Guides review of common project configuration files before drafting.
Identifies reusable components from source folders and project documentation.
Creates design goals, feature lists, and scoped interaction flows.
Produces Mermaid sequence diagrams for main user and service flows.
Outlines implementation approaches, key methods, and technical challenges.
Adds data model and API sections when the design needs them.
limitations: It does not implement production code or run tests.
It needs project files or clear user context for accurate output.
Generated designs still need review by the responsible engineering team.
It may state assumptions when repository context is incomplete.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Feature
use_cases.description: Create a focused design document before a sprint starts.

use_cases.title: Document a Service Change
use_cases.description: Summarize flow changes, data changes, and implementation steps for a backend module.

use_cases.title: Align Product and Engineering
use_cases.description: Turn product requirements into a short technical plan with clear scope.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a short feature idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an agile design document for this feature: [describe feature]. Keep it MVP-focused and concise.

prompt_templates.title: Use Repository Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request inside an existing project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this project context, identify the stack, and draft a design document for [feature or module]. Reuse existing components where possible.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Sprint Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed feature scope and produce a lean design document. Mark optional work for later iterations.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Design Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with multiple implementation paths.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an agile design document for [feature]. Compare two implementation options, choose one, and explain the tradeoffs clearly.

output_examples.input: A team needs a design document for user invitations.
output_examples.output: A concise document with design goals, feature list, invitation flow, reusable services, API notes, and MVP boundaries.

output_examples.input: A backend developer wants to change notification delivery.
output: A summary of affected services and existing components.
A sequence flow for request handling and delivery.
Implementation notes, data changes, and technical risks.

output_examples.input: A product manager wants engineering alignment before sprint planning.
output_examples.output: A short technical plan that separates core requirements, optional work, open questions, and review points.

best_practices: Provide the feature goal, user flow, and known constraints before asking for the document.
Let the assistant inspect project configuration and existing modules when available.
Review assumptions and optional items with the team before implementation starts.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a broad architecture redesign when only one feature is needed.
Do not skip project context if the design must integrate with existing code.
Do not treat generated examples as final production code.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates concise technical design documents for agile software teams.

faq.question: Does it write production code?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples, but engineers must build and test the final code.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the feature goal, repository context, constraints, and any existing components that should be reused.

faq.question: Can it use an existing repository?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to inspect project structure and common configuration files when the tool can access them.

faq.question: How does it avoid overdesign?
faq.answer: It prioritizes MVP scope, separates optional work, and keeps each section focused on implementation decisions.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Developers, technical leads, and product managers can use it to align on feature implementation plans.
